recipes.name: Exquisite Pizza Sauce
ingredients_raw: 6 fluid ounces warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)

steps.text: Place tomato paste, water, Parmesan cheese, honey, garlic, anchovy paste, onion powder, oregano, marjoram, basil, black pepper, cayenne pepper, red pepper flakes, and salt into a medium bowl; mix until well blended, breaking up any clumps of cheese.
Set sauce aside for 30 minutes to allow the flavors to blend; spread over pizza dough and prepare pizza as desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Exquisite Pizza Sauce
raw_recipe.description: The best pizza sauces are homemade, just like this flavorful no-cook recipe made with tomato paste, garlic, Parmesan, anchovy paste, herbs, and spices.

review.reviewBody: I've used this recipe many, many times -- we love it. I actually use it so much, I put together a big batch of all the dry ingredients so I don't have to measure out all the spices every time (let alone go searching my pantry to find them every time)... I multiplied all the dry ingredients (onion powder through red pepper flakes) by 8 (eg, 1/4 tsp becomes 2 tsp, 1/8 is 1 tsp, etc), mixed them all up, and store them in a small jar -- every time I want to make the sauce, I just have to measure out 2 tsp of the dry ingredients.

We love this recipe!

Hint: For easy/quick prep, scale this recipe to 40 and combine the dry spices in a spice jar. Whenever you want fresh sauce, use appx. 1 tablespoon of the mixture in the regular recipe.

I made this recipe as is the first time, omitting the anchovy paste. We found it to be much too sweet and a little too oniony. Made it a second time using 1 tsp of honey rather than 2 tbsp and it was much better. Also used romano cheese rather than parmesean, and only used 1/2 tsp onion powder. Instead of adding dried herbs, we mixed the other ingredients together in a sauce pan and submerged a sprig each of fresh basil and oregano in the tomato mixture. Simmered for just a few minutes and then discarded the herb sprigs. We ended up with smooth tomato texture with a nice fresh herb taste. Don't simmer too long or the herb taste will be too overpowering! This sauce also has a kick when you cut back on the honey. Next time we'll do 1/8 tsp crushed red pepper *or* cayenne, not both. But we'll definitely make it again!

I added a few tablespoons of white wine to the warm water, which adds a wonderful flavor. Remember that the honey and peppers balance each other out, so if you follow other reviewers' suggestions and reduce the honey, you should also reduce the peppers -- unless you like your sauce very spicy. I use half the honey and use only half the black and cayenne pepper, and omit the red pepper flakes. I also double the oregano for a genuine pizzeria flavor.

Use this recipe for a pizza bar party with 35 guests. I multiplied everything by 7 (idk it just felt right) and still had enough leftover to fill an 8oz mason jar. I couldn’t find anchovy paste at Kroger so I used 5 whole anchovies and made the sauce in my Vitamix. Every raved about it and said not to change a thing. I also only used about 75% of the honey. I think the Parmesan provided a nice balance to the sweetness of the honey. Also do not omit the anchovies.

I tested on a very small homemade pizza and it was great so today I am making two large pizzas. I took the advice to multiply the dry ingredients by eight and I have them in a jar and that way when I want to make this wonderful pizza sauce again it’s already all there at the wet ingriedence.

I made it with ingredients on hand which included tomato sauce, paste and San Mateo whole tomatoes I pureed. All remaining ingdients as written. I made a double batch and canned the remainder the next day. I'll be making this recipe from now on. We loved it!

I don't know why I didn't pay attention to my own intuition when I saw that this recipe called for 2 *tablespoons* of honey. If there's one thing I don't like it's sweet pizza sauce. Pizza is savory, not sweet, and this sauce clashes with typical pizza ingredients such as pepperoni, sausage, cheeses, kalamata olives, pesto, etc. The only reason it gets three stars rather than two is because the spicyness (which works well with those ingredients I just listed) is a nice touch that the family liked. I'd try this again with maybe 1-2 teaspoons of honey rather that the 2 tablespoons (that's 6 teaspoons!) that the recipe calls for.

I googled 2 other sauce recipes tonight and threw them both out. I found this one and it was delicious. I doubled the recipe as I had a bigger tin of tomato paste. The only change I made was to sub sugar for honey as I don't care for it. Maybe I added a bit more hot pepper flakes cuz we love spicey. Next time I will add some fennel. This is a super easy, pantry friendly sauce and is so good. Thanks for the recipe
Wow... I’ve never reviewed a recipe before but don’t want anyone else to ruin a pizza. You definitely don’t want to add 2 tablespoons of honey - maybe 2 teaspoons at most.

This is awesome. I make it often. And my pizza-loving crew noticed the time when I didn't. 
Just made it again tonight. I'm sure it will be well-received as usual. 
In my latest minor variation, I once again substituted a teaspoon of fish sauce instead of anchovy paste, and although the recipe is no-cook, I mix it all in a saucepan and heat it (low) while blending. This time I added about an ounce of red wine and let it simmer down (med-low) to cook it out. The extra moisture helped blend things even easier in the pan, too.
I've been using this recipe since 2014, really that says it all. I would like to thank Angie for sharing, as it's a staple in my kitchen and can always be found in my fridge.
Very tasty. I did not use anchovy paste and cut honey in half. Otherwise followed recipe.
Have used this recipe for years. People ask if I will share my secret recipe 😀
good combination of spices to add flavor to your pizza
Wow, great sauce! Easy, fast. You can make a head as well, and no cooking is awesome. Everything in your pantry. Will be putting this and the pizza dough recipe into our dinner rotation!
We loved this sauce. I followed the recipe except did not add anchovy paste.
This was not only simple, but delicious! I didn't have any anchovy paste, but I'm betting it's even better with it. I think I'll double it next time and freeze what I don't use.

My husband and I are not fans ..I only used 1/2 the honey because I don’t like sweet sause. I also didn’t have marjoram, but other than that I followed the recipe. I won’t make it again, there are too many others I enjoy more.
